title: test(plugin-grid,console): pin the members of object-grid's four toolbar keys (objectui#8071 slice 13)
body:
Refs #8071 — slice 13. At least seven exemptions remain after this one, so the card stays open; this PR is deliberately written with no closing keyword anywhere in it.

Clause-②: no

## What this slice does

Four `object-grid` keys leave `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` and enter `MEMBER_PINS`, and `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` moves to the new count in the same commit: **`batchActions`, `pagination`, `searchableFields`, `selection`**.

It also repairs five figures in `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` that had rotted into present-tense claims about shared, ratcheting constants.

## The batch, and why it is this one

The dispatch deliberately did not name a batch. It handed over slice 12's reading and asked for one chosen by where the **reads** cluster. The constant was re-taken by this seat from the declaration itself, on `origin/main` `26ac50369`, before the first edit — not from the card's prose list, which its own dated block says is stale in both directions.

`object-grid` held eleven. Four of the eleven are the ones slice 12 already read and ruled one-slice-each (`columns` pulls in the column fold and the `$select` projection; `grouping` pulls in `useGroupedData`; `filter` and `sort` each carry dedicated files that need reading end to end). That leaves seven, and four of those seven are **one read**:

`ObjectGrid.tsx` resolves all four inside the single fold that assembles the `data-table` props, and each is the canonical half of a canonical-vs-deprecated pair nothing had asserted the precedence of:

| key | read as | deprecated sibling it outranks |
|---|---|---|
| `pagination` | `schema.pagination !== undefined`, then `.pageSize` / `.pageSizeOptions` | `showPagination`, flat `pageSize` |
| `searchableFields` | `!== undefined ? length is positive : showSearch` | `showSearch` |
| `selection` | `schema.selection?.type` | `selectable` |
| `batchActions` | `schema.batchActions ?? schema.bulkActions` | (it IS the legacy half; its result feeds `selection`'s last fallback arm) |

`batchActions` is in the batch because its result is what `hasBulkActions` reads, and `hasBulkActions` is the third arm of the very chain `selection` is pinned on. The four meet at one gate. Three files, two of them promotions after growth.

The three keys left behind on this block after this slice — `aggregations`, `dataSource`, `navigation` — plus the four slice 12 ruled, are the seven that remain.

## The finding the clustering surfaced

**Two adjacent object-armed keys on one block read their own presence in opposite ways**, and neither description says so. `pagination` is read as `!== undefined`, so the object's presence alone enables paging and overrules `showPagination: false`. `selection` is read as `?.type`, so the object's presence alone does nothing at all. That asymmetry is now pinned from both sides with its controls.

## Consequences an author suffers, named

- **`selection`** — a grid declaring `bulkActions: ['approve']` and `selection: { type: 'none' }` renders with no checkbox in it. `none` is an explicit off that beats *both* fallback arms, including the auto-enable the bulk-action declaration would otherwise trigger. The bar the author declared can never be populated; nothing is thrown, nothing is logged, and the schema reads as configured.
- **`pagination`** — `pageSizeOptions` REPLACES the built-in rows-per-page list rather than extending it. An author who adds `pageSizeOptions: [200]` to offer one larger step silently deletes 5 / 10 / 20 / 50 / 100 from the selector. The control still renders and still works; it simply no longer offers what it offered yesterday.
- **`searchableFields`** — an empty array is not "narrow nothing", it is search **off**: the toolbar box disappears. An author who empties the list while re-picking fields loses the control, not the narrowing.
- **`batchActions`** — a schema half-migrated to `bulkActions` that leaves `batchActions: []` behind loses every bulk action. The checkboxes still tick and the selection bar still counts; only the buttons are missing.

## Every pin shown FAILING, with the restore proven

Five ablations. Each mutates the read site toward the plausible improvement, proves the mutation reached disk (anchor and injected text each counted before and after — a zero-hit edit tool exits 0 and would otherwise read as a run), runs the three pin files, then restores from `HEAD` under a trap and proves the restore by blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`. Target blob at `HEAD`: `552dc5a51f97698a655f7771b7b9507658dba7ca`; every leg restored to exactly that.

| mutation applied to the read site | vitest exit | tests red | which |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefer the deprecated flat `pageSize` over `pagination.pageSize` | 1 | 1 of 28 | `pagination.pageSize` WINS over the deprecated flat `pageSize` |
| drop the `pageSizeOptions` pass-through, always use the built-in list | 1 | 1 of 28 | `pageSizeOptions` REPLACES the built-in rows-per-page list |
| read `type: 'none'` as no opinion, fall through to the legacy/auto arms | 1 | 2 of 28 | `none` is an explicit OFF that beats the bulk-action auto-enable; `none` also beats the deprecated `selectable: true` |
| let an EMPTY `searchableFields` fall through to `showSearch` | 1 | 1 of 28 | an EMPTY `searchableFields` turns the search box OFF |
| fall through to `bulkActions` when the legacy array is EMPTY | 1 | 1 of 28 | an EMPTY `batchActions` still wins — a declared `[]` is a VALUE, not an absence |

**One reading was refused by its own ablation, and the prose was corrected rather than the ablation retried until it agreed.** The `batchActions` pin first said the empty array survives *because the coalesce is nullish*. Swapping `??` for `||` left all 28 tests green: an empty array is both non-nullish AND truthy, so the two operators are indistinguishable here. The docblock in `bulkActionsSpecKey.test.tsx` and the `pins` prose in the ledger now say that explicitly, and the recorded mutation is the one that actually can fail it — an explicit length test, which is the repair a reader would really reach for.

## Set identity and the ceiling, in the same commit

Read out of the diff, not asserted:

- leaving `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS`: `object-grid.batchActions`, `object-grid.pagination`, `object-grid.searchableFields`, `object-grid.selection`
- entering `MEMBER_PINS`: the same four, nothing else, in either direction
- `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING`: `20` to `16` on one line of the same commit, and the live declaration below it holds exactly 16 entries

Both readings were taken at `26ac50369`, which is this branch's base **and** `origin/main` at push time — no merge intervened, so no count here spans one.

## The prose repair — as a rule or a dated reading, never today's number

Five figures repaired. Each had become a present-tense claim about a constant that ratchets under every later slice, which is the defect objectui#9781 names and repairs; writing today's value in would author it a third time this shift.

| rotted text, re-taken from the file | repaired as |
|---|---|
| "and the reason `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` reads 62" | a DATED reading: objectui#8176 RAISED it — the one raise this constant has had — plus an explicit note that the number is deliberately not restated because it only ratchets down |
| "`MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` stays 62" | a RULE: it DID NOT MOVE for those keys; "a new array key gets a pin, never room" is what survives, the number is the declaration's |
| "lists all 50 remaining keys BY NAME" | a RULE: lists EVERY remaining key by name — the list IS the census, so read it rather than any count written about it |
| "the cheap way to green a new array key is to add a 51st entry" | "…is to add ONE MORE entry", with the assertion that refuses it named |
| "cannot be absorbed by adding a 51st entry" | "…by adding ONE MORE entry", plus a note that neither the count nor the ceiling is written into that docblock |

A sixth in the same class was repaired opportunistically while the file was open: `AWAITING_A_PIN`'s docblock opened "One shared constant rather than 58 near-copies", which reads as a live count of the list. It now says "rather than one near-copy per entry"; the measured population size stays in the string below it, where it is attributed to the card that measured it.

## Files

- **NEW** `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridPagerSelectionMembers-8071.test.tsx` — `pagination` and `selection`. Neither had a file constraining its members at the grid. `groupedPagination.test.tsx` names the block and the key and would satisfy a string locator, but its subject is GROUP paging and its one `pagination` fixture exists to suppress a pager; `data-table-selection-mode.test.tsx` pins the vocabulary one layer down and never names `object-grid`, so this repo's own locator would have refused it. Neither was credited.
- **GROWN, then promoted** `serverSearch.test.tsx` — `searchableFields`. Its ADR-0061 row really does pin the key's forwarding, a genuine near miss, but with a single-member array and no arity row. Grown by ordering (a deliberately non-alphabetical pair), the empty-array arm, and the precedence over `showSearch: false`.
- **GROWN, then promoted** `bulkActionsSpecKey.test.tsx` — `batchActions`. Its whole subject IS the alias precedence, but both fixtures are non-empty, so the empty-array arm was unstated. Grown by that row and by the auto-enable row.
- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — the four registrations, the four deletions, the ceiling, the slice-13 accounting section, the prose repairs.
- `.changeset/8071-grid-toolbar-member-pins-slice-13.md` — empty frontmatter.

## A member with no read site, reported rather than frozen into the pin

**The GROUPED pager ignores both `pagination` members.** `ObjectGrid`'s own grouped pager hard-codes its rows-per-page choices and reads neither `pagination.pageSize` nor `pagination.pageSizeOptions`, so an authored `pageSizeOptions` reaches the flat pager and is dropped the moment `grouping` is authored. The pin asserts the flat path and says in its own prose that it does. Slice 9's choice, for slice 9's reason: an assertion that a member is dead has to be deleted before anyone can make it live. Handed back as a finding; no card filed from this seat.

## Changeset grade, MEASURED

Empty frontmatter, and measured rather than assumed. Both affected packages were built and their `files[]` entries grepped for symbols this diff introduces, each with a lit control drawn from the same probed population:

| package | published paths probed | probes (symbols this diff adds) | lit controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@object-ui/plugin-grid` | `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE` | `gridPagerSelectionMembers` 0 · "the coalesce is nullish" 0 · "an EMPTY member list disables search" 0 | `pageSizeOptions` 9 · `resolveRowCrudAffordances` 9 · `searchableFields` 16 · `batchActions` 4 |
| `@object-ui/console` | `dist`, `plugin.ts`, `plugin.js`, `plugin.d.ts`, `README.md` | `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` 0 · `MEMBER_PINS` 0 · `gridPagerSelectionMembers` 0 | `object-grid` 21 · `searchableFields` 26 · `pageSizeOptions` 10 |

Every probe zero, every control lit in the same files. Nothing this diff adds reaches published output. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` agrees and prints so.

Exit codes captured to disk before any pipe, in every case.

| run | command-exit | reading |
|---|---|---|

**Typecheck coverage proven non-vacuous.** `tsc -p packages/plugin-grid/tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists 1729 files; all three grid pin files appear exactly once each. The listing discriminates rather than swallowing everything: `plugin-detail` test files 0, the console ledger file 0. The console's own `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` lists 3765 files including the ledger file exactly once, with `gridPagerSelectionMembers` 0 and any `packages/*/__tests__/` 0.

**Lint: a narrowing, declared, with the three readings that make it a measurement.** ① The population is read from eslint's own config, not guessed: `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` minus that config's `ignores` block (`dist`, `.next`, `node_modules`, `public`, `.source`, plus its three literal build artefacts) — 4926 tracked files. ② Files actually linted, counted out of `--format json`: 4, the whole diff's lintable surface. 0 errors, 16 warnings, every one of them `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` on the `as any` fixture casts these files already used; the lines this diff ADDS contribute 4 such occurrences, 3 of them the standard `hasPointerCapture` / `scrollIntoView` / `schema: any` fixture spelling. ③ Invariance for the 4922 untouched files: `eslint.config.js` declares `projectService` 0 times, `project:` 0 times and `tsconfigRootDir` 0 times — linting is not type-aware here, so each file's verdict is computed from that file alone and nothing in this diff can move a verdict on a file it does not contain. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run is CI's.

## Serial constraint

Re-taken over the open-PR set before the first write, not inherited: all 16 open pull requests were listed and each one's file list fetched. Zero of the 16 touch `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`.

⚠️ After that reading the dispatching seat reported a collision it had missed: **objectui#9833** (card objectui#9779) touches the same ledger file, +1/−1, in the `object-form.sections` entry's `pins:` prose inside `MEMBER_PINS`. Re-read at push time: it has **not** landed — `origin/main` is still `26ac50369`, byte-identical to this branch's base on that file. So this pushes unmerged, as instructed, and the enqueue-time conflict is the dispatching seat's to take.

For whoever merges the two: this diff does not touch the `object-form.sections` entry. Its insertions into `MEMBER_PINS` are `object-grid.batchActions` (before the `object-grid.exportOptions` entry) and the `object-grid.pagination` / `searchableFields` / `selection` trio (before the `object-kanban.cardFields` entry). `object-form.sections` sits a couple of entries above the first of those, so the two edits are near but not on the same lines. ⛔ Do not revert objectui#9833's line while merging — it is a deliberate repair of a sentence describing the old behaviour.

## Out of scope, noted and not filed

- The grouped pager's two ignored `pagination` members, above. Successor: this card's next `object-grid` slice, which has to read the grouping path for `grouping` and `aggregations` anyway.
- `ObjectGrid`'s `pageSize` resolution uses `||`, so a member of `0` falls through to the flat key and then to the built-in default. Not a defect anyone can reach (a page size of zero is not authorable in any useful sense) and not pinned. Successor: none.
